properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vagrant/Ansible multi-host demo setup script for the Fabric docker-compose demo; scp with StrictHostKeyChecking=no disables host-key authentication on every copy between the demo VMs. Real posture control, changeable here, but demo/lab infrastructure rather than production.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 used as a record-key/UUID generator in the chaincode and as a digest in the Fabric client app; also a declared dependency in app/api-oracle/package.json. Weak hash in live code paths — not a false match.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.3 ships the SHA-1/SHA-2 family; pulled in transitively (by elliptic) in both lockfiles. This is the dependency inventory: the build ships these hashes whether or not the app calls them directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA on secp256k1 in the EVM smart contracts this repo deploys: the solcInputs embed the OpenZeppelin ECDSA.sol source (ecrecover on secp256k1) used by DAOToken/Governor/NetEmissionsTokenNetwork/CarbonTracker across all testnets, and package-lock.json declares the elliptic/secp256k1 JS libraries that sign on the client side. The curve is fixed by the EVM protocol — observable here, replaceable only by the chain, not by this project.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey npm package (implements OpenSSL's EVP_BytesToKey, an MD5-based legacy KDF) declared throughout the root package-lock.json as a dependency of browserify-aes/browserify-cipher/browserify-des — the crypto-browserify stack that webpack substitutes for node:crypto in the frontend bundle. Dependency inventory: the build ships this weak KDF; changeable here by upgrading the browser polyfill chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two distinct AES-256-CBC uses: (1) demo RSA private keys in app/supply-chain/*.pem stored passphrase-encrypted with the legacy OpenSSL 'traditional' PEM envelope (DEK-Info: AES-256-CBC), unauthenticated CBC; (2) live createCipheriv/createDecipheriv('aes-256-cbc') in data/src/repositories/common.ts (encrypting stored wallet/key material) and the cipher option in lib/supply-chain/src/crypto-utils.ts. Malleable without a separate MAC; changeable here (AES-256-GCM).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA keypair generation in the supply-chain crypto-utils library — classical PKE, Shor-vulnerable. Also a declared dependency reference in the root package-lock.json (node-forge/elliptic chain). Changeable here: swap to ML-KEM-768 when migrating.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Wallet password hashing in the data layer: pbkdf2Sync(password, salt, 1000, 64, 'sha512') — 1000 iterations is far below the OWASP 600k minimum, and these are the password verifiers that guard user wallets (which hold real token balances). Changeable here; raise iterations or move to Argon2id.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Split verdict recorded at site level: the hardhat/test/token-request-integration-tests.ts:52 site is a genuine hardcoded test-account private key (well-known Anvil/Hardhat dev key, test-only but committed material — the pattern to fix), while the fabric/typescript_app/tests/e2e.test.ts:19 site was rejected as an identifier-name collision (recordAuditedEmissionToken is a chaincode function-route mapping, not a secret). Object confirmed on the strength of the real site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA is the signature backbone of this codebase: (1) Fabric CA configs select algo: ecdsa for enrollment certs (auditor1-3, live config); (2) the deployed EVM contracts verify ECDSA/secp256k1 signatures (Governor delegateBySig, TxVerifier.verifySignature in NetEmissionsTokenNetwork) — the ABI metadata sites document those deployed functions; (3) secure-identities signs and verifies with ECDSA at runtime — ws-wallet/src/wallet.ts:273-275 does ecdsa.keyFromPrivate + ecdsa.sign with the elliptic l

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 key agreement in the supply-chain crypto-utils library: keys are labelled with the libsodium 'x25519-xsalsa20-poly1305' format string (tweetnacl/stablelib secretbox stack) at crypto-utils.ts:18/:32, and @stablelib/x25519 is a declared dependency in the root lockfile. Real classical key agreement, retroactively breakable; changeable here (ML-KEM-768 hybrid).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 declared in the Fabric chaincode lockfile — the chaincode vendors lib/supply-chain's crypto-utils, which uses tweetnacl for the x25519-xsalsa20-poly1305 record encryption; Ed25519 is part of tweetnacl's API surface that ships with it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 (X25519 scalar multiplication) declared in the Fabric chaincode lockfile; the chaincode's emissions-record encryption path uses the x25519-xsalsa20-poly1305 construction from lib/supply-chain crypto-utils. Shor-vulnerable key agreement; changeable here via ML-KEM-768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (SHA-3 family, pre-standard padding) is the EVM's native hash: the deployed contracts use it for EIP-712 typehashes, delegation digests, EIP-1967 storage slots and transfer-request hashing across every testnet deployment folder (arbitrum_kovan, avalanche-testnet, bsctestnet, goerli, hedera-testnet, xdai), plus keccak/js-sha3 in the lockfiles for off-chain hashing. Fixed by the EVM protocol — observable here, replaceable only by the chain; Grover-only exposure, low urgency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 used as a key-derivation step in the data layer's field encryption: createHash('sha256').update(FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY).digest('base64').substr(0,32) produces the AES-256-CBC key that encrypts stored records. Live op chain; the KDF-from-env-secret design is itself notable but the hash is SHA-256.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.1.1 declared in the root package-lock.json — dependency inventory; supplies SHA-256 among others to the shipped build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305) declared in the Fabric chaincode lockfile — the AE used to seal emissions records in the chaincode's encryption path. Quantum-safe symmetric AE; kept as inventory, no PQ action needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js is a declared dependency of app/api-oracle, the emissions-record chaincode, and the root build — the chaincode uses its MD5 export to build record UUIDs (emissionsRecordContract.ts:73). Ships MD5/SHA/AES/ECDSA primitives; the weak-MD5 call site is the live use found so far.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge declared in the root lockfile — ships RSA/PKCS/X.509 TLS implementations to the build; available in the shipped library, no call site found in the application itself.

properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto@v0.0.0-20190308221718 pinned in the datalock Go chaincode's go.sum — a 2019 snapshot that predates all PQ work and carries the classical KEX/ssh/bcrypt packages. Dependency inventory for the Go chaincode; changeable here by bumping the module version.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ssh2@1.11.0 declared in the root package-lock.json — SSH protocol implementation available to the build. Its 1.11.0 KEX set (curve25519-sha256, ecdh-sha2-nistp*, diffie-hellman-group14) is classical; no PQ KEX is offered at this version. No application call site found; presence is the inventory question here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-vault@0.9.22 is how the Fabric client app reaches HashiCorp Vault's transit engine for TX signing (LEDGER_FABRIC_TX_SIGNER='vault', LEDGER_FABRIC_TX_SIGNER_VAULT_MOUNT='transit' in .env). This is the key-management-infrastructure asset: the signing keys live in Vault, outside this repo, and the algorithms Vault transit offers (RSA-2048+, ECDSA P-256/P-384, ed25519 — no PQ at typical versions) decide the posture. Observable here; replaceable only via the Vault server's crypto library.
